title: Bessent Downplays Worries on Rising Yields, AI Bubble Concerns
source_used: Bloomberg (text read on the Yahoo Finance copy); Investing.com version also read on Yahoo Finance
key_facts: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in an Axios interview published Saturday 3 Oct 2026, said the rise in US Treasury yields tracks a global move and is not a US-specific problem
The 10-year Treasury yield briefly hit its highest since 2002 this week; mortgage rates are above 7 percent
Bessent dismissed talk of an AI bubble, saying Microsoft, Google and Meta are investing heavily and producing strong revenue growth for Anthropic and OpenAI
Bloomberg lists fuel prices from the Iran war, US fiscal worries and surging AI spending as drivers of higher borrowing costs
Bessent defended the US rescue of Argentina (a $20 billion swap line) and said similar rescues are possible
Friday's soft US jobs data gave bonds some relief
quote_evidence: "I would be concerned if we were having some kind of idiosyncratic rise," Bessent said during an interview with Axios published on Saturday.
"I can't control the bond market. What I can do is get people to slow down and think," he said.

The secretary also dismissed concerns about an AI-driven bubble, arguing that key players such as Microsoft Corp. Alphabet Inc.'s Google and Meta Platforms Inc. are investing substantial capital and generating significant revenue growth for the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI.
why_it_matters_hint: The US Treasury chief is publicly rejecting the bubble and bond-stress worries that other officials and investors raised this week
